citations.explanation: An applied substitution records instruction wording edits and mutates the shared equipment set, extending its effect beyond the ingredient row.
The accumulated edits are subsequently replayed in order across both main and component instructions.

reviews.label: sha256-ff492da9389dc03977c99d08fe6f687ec6eb8f66480c863ddbd78af599791fd7
reviews.rationale: The implementation performs ordered whole-recipe wording and equipment edits, but it has no reference/index linking ingredient identity to dependent fields and no unified semantic representation of those dependencies. Ingredient IDs are merely copied into output rows; wording and equipment are independent effect ledgers. The full reference-aware mechanism is therefore absent.

citations.explanation: Each chosen substitution accumulates ordered wording changes and equipment effects outside the ingredient row.
The ordered wording ledger is globally replayed over main and component instructions.

reviews.label: sha256-481a31a13a8928ba50469a3aa7e470683e898f59646e414cf1550b856bdce84d
reviews.rationale: Substitutions produce ordered global instruction and equipment rewrites, but dependent fields are never linked to an ingredient identity or represented in a dependency-aware intermediate model. The code instead maintains separate wording and equipment collections, so it does not implement the required reference-aware transformation.

citations.explanation: A substitution accumulates ordered wording and equipment effects in the pass object.
citations.quote:
p.wording += list(result.get("wording_changes", []))
p.add_equipment += list(result.get("add_equipment", []))
p.remove_equipment += list(result.get("remove_equipment", []))

citations.explanation: The accumulated wording passes are applied to every main and retained-component instruction string.

reviews.label: sha256-8c07cb74d7e95effe3cd73fb87a7ba288a8d7f8dfac95e4dc29a0daf687102c5
reviews.rationale: The pass object supports global rewriting, but it is only a collection of independent effect lists. It contains no ingredient-to-instruction/equipment references or semantic dependency links, and ingredient IDs are not used to target dependent recipe fields. Thus the frozen reference-aware mechanism is not fully instantiated.

citations.explanation: Substitution application records ordered wording edits and modifies shared equipment effects.
The accumulated changes are replayed over top-level and component instructions.
citations.quote:
instructions = _apply_wording(recipe.get("instructions", []),
                              res.wording_changes)
for comp in components:
...
    if "instructions" in comp:
        comp["instructions"] = _apply_wording(comp["instructions"],
                                              res.wording_changes)

reviews.label: sha256-d48b6b5185847aaffa48100c908ecfefa9716bbb2d918a8803779d30be939c26
reviews.rationale: Although substitutions drive ordered instruction and equipment changes, `_Resolution` does not encode references from an ingredient identity to the affected fields. Its separate effect collections are applied indiscriminately across the recipe, so the required linked, reference-aware transformation is missing.

citations.explanation: During substitution, wording changes are globally applied to the instruction list while equipment is also updated.
citations.quote:
for wc in res.get("wording_changes", ()):
    instructions[:] = [line.replace(wc["old"], wc["new"]) for line in instructions]
equipment.update(res.get("add_equipment", ()))
equipment.difference_update(res.get("remove_equipment", ()))

reviews.rationale: A substitution directly rewrites instructions and equipment beyond its ingredient row, but no ingredient identity is linked to those dependent fields. The edits are broad string replacement and set mutation, with no dependency-aware intermediate representation. The full mechanism and frozen correspondence are therefore not established.

citations.explanation: Applied substitution effects are recorded as ordered wording changes and equipment mutations.

reviews.rationale: The implementation propagates substitution effects into instructions and equipment, but it has no explicit ingredient-reference map or semantic dependency model. reviews.rationale: The code has a global ordered rewrite pass, but it does not preserve or build links between ingredient identity and dependent instructions/equipment.
